About the data

  • Everything on this page comes from the NC State Board of Elections' statewide absentee ballot files: one record per one-stop (early, in-person) or mail ballot, for every federal general election from 2002 to 2026. Election Day votes from 2016 on come from the State Board's voter history file. Only accepted ballots count.
  • The 2026 file is refreshed by the State Board early each morning with the previous day's ballots, and this page is rebuilt as soon as a new file is posted.
  • Voters are followed across elections by their State Board voter ID (NCID). Records before 2016 don't carry it and are linked by county and county registration number, so voters who changed counties before 2016 can lose some earlier history.
  • First-time one-stop means no one-stop ballot in any federal general election from 2002 to 2024. Primaries and municipal elections aren't counted.
  • Earlier or later compares how many days before Election Day the ballot was cast. Early voting opened 19 days before Election Day in 2022, 2024 and 2026, so day 1 lines up in all three years.
  • One-stop sites are matched across years by street address from the State Board's published site lists.
  • This page shows totals only, never individual voters.
This page uses data from the North Carolina State Board of Elections but is not affiliated with or endorsed by it.
